1	﻿# Localization Architecture
     2	
     3	> Comprehensive guide to the zero-hardcoding localization system
     4	
     5	---
     6	
     7	## Table of Contents
     8	
     9	1. [Zero-Hardcoding Design](#zero-hardcoding-design)
    10	2. [Chinese and Japanese Translation Guidelines](#chinese-and-japanese-translation-guidelines)
    11	3. [Locale File Structure](#locale-file-structure)
    12	4. [Language Preference System](#language-preference-system)
    13	5. [Adding a New Language](#adding-a-new-language)
    14	6. [Testing LocalizationService](#testing-localizationservice)
    15	
    16	---
    17	
    18	## Zero-Hardcoding Design
    19	
    20	The localization system uses a **zero-hardcoding architecture** where adding a new language requires **only a JSON file**:
    21	
    22	```json
    23	{
    24	  "LocaleName": "Português (Brasil)",
    25	  "ParentCulture": "pt",
    26	  "MainWindow": { "key": "translated value" },
    27	  "Settings": { "key": "translated value" }
    28	}
    29	```
    30	
    31	No C# code changes, no compilation, no hardcoded mappings. The system automatically:
    32	- Discovers new locale files via file system scanning
    33	- Reads display names from `LocaleName` property
    34	- Maps parent cultures via `ParentCulture` property
    35	- Populates language dropdown dynamically
    36	- Supports automatic system locale detection
    37	
    38	### Supported Languages
    39	
    40	- **Total Languages**: 8
    41	- **Locale Codes**: en-US, de-DE, fr-FR, es-ES, it-IT, zh-CN, ja-JP, pt-BR
    42	- **Total Strings**: 201 translated strings per locale 
    43	- **User-Selectable**: Language preference dropdown in Settings
    44	- **Auto-Detection**: Automatic system locale detection
    45	- **Extensibility**: New languages require only JSON file (no code changes)
    46	
    47	---
    48	
    49	## Chinese and Japanese Translation Guidelines
    50	
    51	**Critical formatting rules for Asian language translations** (zh-CN, ja-JP):
    52	
    53	### 1. Menu Hotkeys Placement
    54	
    55	- Place hotkeys at the **end** of menu items using the format `(_X)`
    56	- Example (Chinese): `"FileMenuHeader": "文件(_F)"`
    57	- Example (Japanese): `"FileMenuHeader": "ファイル(_F)"`
    58	- **Do NOT** place space before hotkey parentheses in menu items
    59	
    60	### 2. Aki Spacing (空き)
    61	
    62	- **Always maintain spacing** between English words/numbers and Asian characters
    63	- Correct: `版本 {0}` or `JSON 形式`
    64	- Incorrect: `版本{0}` or `JSON形式`
    65	- This improves scannability and follows modern UI typography standards
    66	
    67	### 3. Quotation Marks
    68	
    69	- Use **Chinese quotes** `" "` (zh-CN) when referring to folder names or UI labels
    70	- Use **Japanese quotes** `「 」` (ja-JP) when referring to folder names or UI labels
    71	- Example (Chinese): `"Profiles" 文件夹`
    72	- Example (Japanese): `「Profiles」フォルダ`
    73	
    74	### 4. Punctuation
    75	
    76	- Use **full-width punctuation** for all descriptive text
    77	- Chinese: `， 。 ： （ ）` instead of `, . : ( )`
    78	- Japanese: Already uses full-width by default
    79	- Example (Chinese): `列表中有很多更改，包括替换和移除。`
    80	- Maintains visual consistency with Asian character blocks
    81	
    82	### 5. Technical Terms
    83	
    84	- Keep technical proper nouns (SFSE, Vanilla, GitHub, etc.) in English
    85	- Surround with full-width parentheses when needed
    86	- Example (Japanese): `プレイ（SFSE）`
    87	- Example (Chinese): `开始游戏（SFSE）`
    88	
    89	### Typography Anti-Patterns to Avoid
    90	
    91	- ❌ Western punctuation in Chinese text: `列表中有很多更改, 包括替换和移除.`
    92	- ❌ Missing spacing: `版本{0}` or `JSON格式`
    93	- ❌ Western quotes: `'Profiles' 文件夹` (use `"Profiles"` instead)
    94	- ❌ Space before hotkey: `文件 (_F)` (use `文件(_F)` instead)
    95	
    96	---
    97	
    98	## Locale File Structure
    99	
   100	Each locale file (`en-US.json`, `de-DE.json`, etc.) contains:

101	
   102	### Root-Level Metadata
   103	
   104	Used by `LocalizationService`:
   105	
   106	- `LocaleName`: Native language name (e.g., "Deutsch", "Français")
   107	- `ParentCulture`: Two-letter ISO 639-1 code (e.g., "de", "fr")
   108	
   109	### Translation Sections
   110	
   111	Used by ViewModels:
   112	
   113	| Section | Purpose |
   114	|---------|---------|
   115	| `MainWindow` | Main window strings |
   116	| `Menu` | Menu and status bar strings |
   117	| `Settings` | Settings window strings |
   118	| `ErrorDialog` | Error dialog strings |
   119	| `About` | About window strings |
   120	| `DiffDialog` | Load order changes dialog strings |
   121	| `ManageProfiles` | Profile management window strings |
   122	| `ProfileProperties` | Profile creation/editing strings |
   123	| `SwitchProfile` | Profile switching dialog strings |
   124	| `ReferenceHistory` | Reference version history strings |
   125	| `UpdateOptions` | Update download options strings |
   126	| `ViewPendingChanges` | Pending changes window strings |
   127	| `CommentInput` | Comment input dialog strings |
   128	| `ConfirmationDialog` | Generic confirmation dialog strings |
   129	| `Common` | Shared strings across dialogs |
   130	| `StatusCoordinator` | Status message strings |
   131	| `FileMonitoring` | File monitoring warning strings |
   132	| `ConfigInvalidOverlay` | Configuration overlay strings |
   133	| `MainWindowStatus` | Main window status message strings |
   134	| `ViewModelInitializerStatus` | Application initialization status strings |
   135	| `ReferenceManagementStatus` | Reference file management status strings |
   136	
   137	---
   138	
   139	## Language Preference System
   140	
   141	### User-Facing Features
   142	
   143	- Language dropdown in Settings window (9 options: Automatic + 8 languages)
   144	- Automatic system locale detection (when set to "Automatic")
   145	- Persistence across application restarts
   146	- Restart notification banner when language changes
   147	
   148	### Configuration
   149	
   150	- **Storage**: `config.json` as `PreferredLanguage` property
   151	- **Values**: `"auto"` (default), `"en-US"`, `"de-DE"`, `"fr-FR"`, `"es-ES"`, `"it-IT"`, `"zh-CN"`, `"ja-JP"`, `"pt-BR"`
   152	- **Application**: Applied on application startup via `ViewModelInitializer`
   153	
   154	### Implementation Details
   155	
   156	| Component | Purpose |
   157	|-----------|---------|
   158	| `LocalizationService.GetLocaleName()` | Reads native name from JSON |
   159	| `LocalizationService.BuildParentCultureMap()` | Scans all files for parent mappings |
   160	| `LocalizationService.DetectSystemCulture()` | Uses dynamic parent mapping |
   161	| `SettingsViewModel.BuildLanguageList()` | Dynamically populates dropdown |
   162	| `LanguageOption` model | Holds `Code` and `DisplayName` for dropdown |
   163	
   164	---
   165	
   166	## Adding a New Language
   167	
   168	To add a new language (e.g., Portuguese):
   169	
   170	### Step 1: Copy Template
   171	
   172	Copy `en-US.json` to `pt-BR.json` in `ViewTexts\Locales\`
   173	
   174	### Step 2: Set Metadata
   175	
   176	```json
   177	{
   178	  "LocaleName": "Português (Brasil)",
   179	  "ParentCulture": "pt",
   180	  ...
   181	}
   182	```
   183	
   184	### Step 3: Translate Strings
   185	
   186	Translate all string values in each section (189 strings total)
   187	
   188	### Step 4: Configure Build Action (**CRITICAL**)
   189	
   190	Add to `.csproj`:
   191	
   192	```xml
   193	<ItemGroup>
   194	  <Content Include="ViewTexts\Locales\pt-BR.json">
   195	    <CopyToOutputDirectory>PreserveNewest</CopyToOutputDirectory>
   196	  </Content>
   197	</ItemGroup>
   198	```
   199	
   200	### Step 5: Build Application
   201	
   202	Build to include content file in output directory
   203	
   204	### Step 6: Verify
   205	
   206	Check that `bin/.../ViewTexts/Locales/pt-BR.json` exists after build
   207	
   208	### Step 7: Test
   209	
   210	Launch application - language appears in dropdown automatically
   211	
   212	---
   213	
   214	## Common Mistakes
   215	
   216	### ⚠️ Forgetting Build Action Configuration
   217	
   218	**Problem**: File won't be copied during build and language won't appear in dropdown
   219	
   220	**Solution**: Always add `<CopyToOutputDirectory>PreserveNewest</CopyToOutputDirectory>` to `.csproj`
   221	
   222	### ⚠️ Invalid JSON Syntax
   223	
   224	**Problem**: Application fails to load translations
   225	
   226	**Solution**: Validate JSON syntax before committing (use JSON linter)
   227	
   228	### ⚠️ Missing Translation Keys
   229	
   230	**Problem**: UI shows placeholder text or throws errors
   231	
   232	**Solution**: Ensure all 189 keys are present in the file (use en-US.json as reference)
   233	
   234	### ⚠️ Incorrect Metadata
   235	
   236	**Problem**: Language doesn't appear or automatic detection fails
   237	
   238	**Solution**: Verify `LocaleName` and `ParentCulture` are set correctly
   239	
   240	---
   241	
   242	## Technical Architecture
   243	
   244	### Services
   245	
   246	| Service | Role |
   247	|---------|------|
   248	| `LocalizationService` | Singleton managing locale loading and culture detection |
   249	| `LocalizationJsonNormalizer` | Validates and normalizes JSON files |
   250

251	### ViewModels
   252	
   253	15 specialized ViewModels provide localized strings:
   254	
   255	- `MainWindowTexts`
   256	- `MenuTexts`
   257	- `SettingsTexts`
   258	- `ErrorDialogTexts`
   259	- `AboutTexts`
   260	- `DiffDialogTexts`
   261	- `ManageProfilesTexts`
   262	- `ProfilePropertiesTexts`
   263	- `SwitchProfileTexts`
   264	- `ReferenceHistoryTexts`
   265	- `UpdateOptionsTexts`
   266	- `ViewPendingChangesTexts`
   267	- `CommentInputTexts`
   268	- `ConfirmationDialogTexts`
   269	- `CommonTexts`
   270	- `StatusCoordinatorTexts`
   271	- `FileMonitoringTexts`
   272	- `ConfigInvalidOverlayTexts`
   273	- `MainWindowStatusTexts`
   274	- `ViewModelInitializerStatusTexts`
   275	- `ReferenceManagementStatusTexts`
   276	
   277	### Data Flow
   278	
   279	1. **Startup**: `ViewModelInitializer` loads preferred language from `config.json`
   280	2. **Detection**: If set to "auto", `LocalizationService.DetectSystemCulture()` determines locale
   281	3. **Loading**: `LocalizationService` loads JSON file and populates ViewModels
   282	4. **Binding**: UI elements bind to ViewModel properties via XAML
   283	5. **Runtime**: Language changes trigger ViewModel property updates and UI refresh
   284	
   285	---
   286	
   287	## No Code Changes Required
   288	
   289	**Key principle**: Adding a new language requires **only a JSON file**. No C# code changes, no compilation needed for translations.
   290	
   291	The architecture dynamically discovers, loads, and integrates new languages at runtime.
   292	
   293	---
   294	
   295	## Testing LocalizationService
   296	
   297	`LocalizationService` is a **singleton with global mutable state** (`CurrentCulture`). Tests that call `SetCulture()` must isolate their culture changes to avoid corrupting other tests running concurrently or afterward.
   298	
   299	### Test Fixture: EnglishLocaleFixture
   300	
   301	`Tests/LoadOrderKeeper.Tests/Fixtures/EnglishLocaleFixture.cs` provides xUnit fixture support for locale-sensitive tests.
   302	
   303	**What it does:**
   304	- Snapshots `LocalizationService.Instance.CurrentCulture` on construction
   305	- Calls `SetCulture("en-US")` to guarantee English strings for all tests in the consuming class
   306	- Restores the original culture in `Dispose()`
   307	
   308	**Required usage pattern — both mechanisms are mandatory:**
   309	
   310	```csharp
   311	[Collection(LocaleSequentialCollection.Name)]          // (1) Prevents parallel class execution
   312	public sealed class MyTests : IClassFixture<EnglishLocaleFixture>  // (2) Per-class fixture lifecycle
   313	{
   314	    public MyTests(EnglishLocaleFixture localeFixture)
   315	    {
   316	        _ = localeFixture; // Ensures en-US culture is active for the lifetime of this test class
   317	        // ... remaining setup
   318	    }
   319	}
   320	```
   321	
   322	| Mechanism | Purpose |
   323	|-----------|---------|
   324	| `IClassFixture<EnglishLocaleFixture>` | Constructs/disposes the fixture once per test class (before first test, after last test). Ensures setup/teardown is bracketed around the class's full run. |
   325	| `[Collection(LocaleSequentialCollection.Name)]` | Groups the class into `LocaleSequentialCollection` which has `DisableParallelization = true`. Prevents concurrent `SetCulture` calls from multiple locale-sensitive test classes running in parallel. |
   326	
   327	**Why both are needed:** `IClassFixture<T>` alone does not prevent xUnit from running test *classes* in parallel. Without `[Collection]`, two classes each have their own fixture instance and can call `SetCulture` concurrently, corrupting the shared singleton and producing intermittent failures.
   328	
   329	### Test Collection: LocaleSequentialCollection
   330	
   331	`Tests/LoadOrderKeeper.Tests/Fixtures/LocaleSequentialCollection.cs` defines the xUnit collection used by all locale-sensitive test classes.
   332	
   333	```csharp
   334	[CollectionDefinition(Name, DisableParallelization = true)]
   335	public class LocaleSequentialCollection
   336	{
   337	    public const string Name = "LocaleSequentialCollection";
   338	}
   339	```
   340	
   341	`DisableParallelization = true` ensures all classes in the collection run sequentially. Use `LocaleSequentialCollection.Name` (not a magic string) in `[Collection]` attributes.
   342	
   343	### Locale-Agnostic Tests
   344	
   345	Tests that observe `LocalizationService` behavior without controlling the culture (e.g., verifying the startup culture detection contract) should **not** use `EnglishLocaleFixture`. These tests must pass on any system locale and should not be placed in `LocaleSequentialCollection`.
   346	
   347	See `LocalizationServiceTests.CurrentCulture_DefaultsToSystemCulture` for the reference implementation: it reads `SessionStartCulture` (immutable after singleton construction) and asserts parseability without mutating singleton state.

    13	5. [Language Preference System](#language-preference-system)
    14	6. [Adding a New Language](#adding-a-new-language)
    15	7. [Testing LocalizationService](#testing-localizationservice)
    16	
    17	---
    18	
    19	## Zero-Hardcoding Design
    20	
    21	The localization system uses a **zero-hardcoding architecture** where adding a new language requires **only a JSON file**:
    22	
    23	```json
    24	{
    25	  "LocaleName": "Português (Brasil)",
    26	  "ParentCulture": "pt",
    27	  "MainWindow": { "key": "translated value" },
    28	  "Settings": { "key": "translated value" }
    29	}
    30	```
    31	
    32	No C# code changes, no compilation, no hardcoded mappings. The system automatically:
    33	- Discovers new locale files via file system scanning
    34	- Reads display names from `LocaleName` property
    35	- Maps parent cultures via `ParentCulture` property
    36	- Populates language dropdown dynamically
    37	- Supports automatic system locale detection
    38	
    39	### Supported Languages
    40	
    41	- **Total Languages**: 8
    42	- **Locale Codes**: en-US, de-DE, fr-FR, es-ES, it-IT, zh-CN, ja-JP, pt-BR
    43	- **Total Strings**: See `en-US.json` for the current key count (use it as the translation template) 
    44	- **User-Selectable**: Language preference dropdown in Settings
    45	- **Auto-Detection**: Automatic system locale detection
    46	- **Extensibility**: New languages require only JSON file (no code changes)
    47	
    48	---
    49	
    50	## Plural Forms — CountFormat / CountSingular Pattern
    51	
    52	Several DiffDialog strings describe counts of mods affected by a load-order change. These use a **paired key convention** to handle the singular/plural distinction without runtime branching in the JSON keys:
    53	
    54	| Key suffix | When used | Example value |
    55	|------------|-----------|---------------|
    56	| `CountFormat` | Count is **2 or more** — contains `{0}` placeholder | `"{0} mod(s) removed"` |
    57	| `CountSingular` | Count is **exactly 1** — no `{0}` placeholder | `"1 mod removed"` |
    58	
    59	### Contract
    60	
    61	- `{0}` in a `CountFormat` value always receives an **integer ≥ 2**. Never pass `1` to a `CountFormat` string; the ViewModel selects `CountSingular` when the count is 1.
    62	- `CountSingular` values **must not** contain `{0}`. The hardcoded `"1"` is intentional.
    63	
    64	### Current key pairs (DiffDialog section)
    65	
    66	```
    67	GuidanceRemovalCountFormat    / GuidanceRemovalCountSingular
    68	GuidanceInsertionCountFormat  / GuidanceInsertionCountSingular
    69	GuidanceReplacementCountFormat/ GuidanceReplacementCountSingular
    70	GuidanceAddedCountFormat      / GuidanceAddedCountSingular
    71	```
    72	
    73	A parallel pair also exists in the confirmation dialog:
    74	
    75	```
    76	ConfirmRiskyDetail_Removals   ({0} placeholder, count ≥ 2)  / ConfirmRiskyDetail_RemovedSingular  (no placeholder)
    77	ConfirmRiskyDetail_Insertions ({0} placeholder, count ≥ 2)  / ConfirmRiskyDetail_InsertedSingular (no placeholder)
    78	```
    79	
    80	### Translator guidance

    84	---
    85	
    86	## Chinese and Japanese Translation Guidelines
    87	
    88	**Critical formatting rules for Asian language translations** (zh-CN, ja-JP):
    89	
    90	### 1. Menu Hotkeys Placement
    91	
    92	- Place hotkeys at the **end** of menu items using the format `(_X)`
    93	- Example (Chinese): `"FileMenuHeader": "文件(_F)"`
    94	- Example (Japanese): `"FileMenuHeader": "ファイル(_F)"`
    95	- **Do NOT** place space before hotkey parentheses in menu items
    96	
    97	### 2. Aki Spacing (空き)
    98	
    99	- **Always maintain spacing** between English words/numbers and Asian characters
   100	- Correct: `版本 {0}` or `JSON 形式`
   101	- Incorrect: `版本{0}` or `JSON形式`
   102	- This improves scannability and follows modern UI typography standards
   103	
   104	### 3. Quotation Marks
   105	
   106	- Use **Chinese quotes** `" "` (zh-CN) when referring to folder names or UI labels
   107	- Use **Japanese quotes** `「 」` (ja-JP) when referring to folder names or UI labels
   108	- Example (Chinese): `"Profiles" 文件夹`
   109	- Example (Japanese): `「Profiles」フォルダ`
   110	
   111	### 4. Punctuation
   112	
   113	- Use **full-width punctuation** for all descriptive text
   114	- Chinese: `， 。 ： （ ）` instead of `, . : ( )`
   115	- Japanese: Already uses full-width by default
   116	- Example (Chinese): `列表中有很多更改，包括替换和移除。`
   117	- Maintains visual consistency with Asian character blocks
   118	
   119	### 5. Technical Terms
   120	
   121	- Keep technical proper nouns (SFSE, Vanilla, GitHub, etc.) in English
   122	- Surround with full-width parentheses when needed
   123	- Example (Japanese): `プレイ（SFSE）`
   124	- Example (Chinese): `开始游戏（SFSE）`
   125	
   126	### Typography Anti-Patterns to Avoid
   127	
   128	- ❌ Western punctuation in Chinese text: `列表中有很多更改, 包括替换和移除.`
   129	- ❌ Missing spacing: `版本{0}` or `JSON格式`
   130	- ❌ Western quotes: `'Profiles' 文件夹` (use `"Profiles"` instead)
